answers.answer: Separate and shuffle assets, demands, events, investments, and each of the five action types. Draw one setup card; place its listed components in each listed district and its stated number of assets facedown one per turn slot from slot 1; then return setup cards. Set round 1, resources 0, reveal demand and set targets. Players choose corporations and matching emergency cards; use the four-player sheet side at four, otherwise five/six. Randomly choose first player, set threat 0; starting capital clockwise is 10, 11, 12, etc. Deal participating corporation rivals plus Federalist, one facedown per player and extra partly under board. Each draws two investments, keeps one facedown, returns the other facedown to deck top.
evidence: Setup (complete setup steps 1–8): the numbered steps specify each deck, city/turn track, tracks, corporations, first player/capital, rivals, and investments.

answers.answer: Four players: Globalsec 2 security then 1 General; Haas-Bioroid 2 labor then 1 General; Jinteki 2 biotech then 1 General; Melange 1 General three times; NBN 2 media then 1 General; Weyland 2 construction then 1 General. Five/six: Globalsec 2 security then 1 media; Haas-Bioroid 2 labor then 1 construction; Jinteki 2 biotech then 1 labor; Melange 1 General three times; NBN 2 media then 1 biotech; Weyland 2 construction then 1 security. Draw top-to-bottom; each General is a separate type not already drawn that Refresh, chosen before seeing cards. Melange therefore uses three different types.
evidence: Corporation draws and contracts: complete corporation table including local headers; preceding paragraph defines operative order and General restrictions.

clauses: Action Phase endpoint and turn availability
answers.answer: At turn start resolve start-of-turn asset abilities, then Refresh by readying exhausted assets and drawing in sheet order. Resolve one deal. At end, use each eligible End of Turn asset ability once in chosen order; newly received assets with that header can also be used this turn. Discard actions down to hand size (normally five; emergencies excluded), then pass left. When the turn track is empty at the end of a turn, the Action Phase ends; the final turn gets its full end step. Some players may have no turn in a round.
evidence: Turn Structure > Standard round and active turn: complete subsection gives the turn sequence and Action Phase endpoint.

answers.answer: Deal steps: reveal the rightmost (highest occupied slot) asset; active player must make a main offer from hand or faceup emergency; other players get one clockwise counteroffer opportunity each; eligible players get one support opportunity each; compare facedown support counts and resolve the winning offer. Main offer wins ties. Resolve the winner's instructions, then the active player claims the revealed asset. Ordinary played actions go facedown to shared discard; emergencies return to their original corporation facedown if they won and faceup otherwise. The active player cannot pass on the main offer.
evidence: Actions > Resolving a deal: complete five numbered steps, including resolution and cleanup.

answers.answer: The first counteroffer costs 0 extra hand cards, the second 1, and the third 2, in addition to each offer. The active player cannot counter without an ability. An earlier displaced counterer is a supporter, because only the active player and current countering player are excluded. There is no second circuit; each other player gets one chance.
evidence: Actions > Resolving a deal, steps 3–4: full counteroffer escalation and support eligibility procedures.

answers.answer: With a counteroffer, everyone except the active and current countering player may support, including a displaced counterer. In turn order, each may support one offer using one or more hand actions facedown beside it, or abstain; emergencies cannot support. A player cannot support both offers or add cards later. The offer with more support cards wins; a 2–2 tie goes to the active player's main offer. With no counteroffer, skip support and the main offer wins by default.
evidence: Actions > Resolving a deal, steps 3–5: complete rules for eligibility, one opportunity, counting, tie, and skipped support.

answers.answer: Only a faceup emergency may be offered as main offer or counteroffer; it cannot support. It is outside the hand, excluded from hand size, and ordinary effects targeting hand actions cannot take/discard it. A stolen emergency returns to its original corporation: facedown if it won an offer, faceup otherwise, including after being offered by another player. Bryan Stinson, when claimed, is discarded to steal two emergency actions from participating corporations; either faceup or facedown, retaining state while stolen.
evidence: Actions > Emergency actions: complete emergency rules and table row for Bryan; Special Rules & Edge Cases > Assets, claiming, exhaustion and theft: Bryan Stinson paragraph.

answers.answer: Development adds 1 to primary production, but orgcrime blocks all primary production; secondary remains available. The district therefore produces 1 entertainment and 0 credits. Protest increases one stage during exploitation, becoming strike. Starting in strike or outage yields no resources. Non-android districts are not exploited in normal Production and produce nothing then.
evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Production, unrest and outages: complete production-modifier table and paragraphs on exploitation and progression.

clauses: Human First outcomes by starting state
answers.answer: From stable, Human First raises unrest two stages to strike. From protest, two stages cannot be added, so place an outage; from strike, unrest cannot increase, so place an outage; from an existing outage, place a new outage and it must move under duplicate-placement rules. An ordinary failed unrest increase without Human First does not create an outage.
evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Production, unrest and outages: Human First paragraph and ordinary cap statement.

answers.answer: The incoming duplicate orgcrime moves along the exiting arrow toward the higher-numbered destination, continuing until it can stay or reaches the Root. In a prisec district, an enemy moves onward; prisec does not remove it. If the unit reaches the Root, return it to reserve and add 2 threat. Movement out of a district is not removal, so it does not trigger a removal contract (including at the Root). Androids instead move to any district, ignoring paths, one at a time, never into a district already containing an android.
evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Placement, movement and the Root: complete subsection covers duplicate placement, prisec, Root, contracts, and android movement.

clauses: action illness trigger and involved districts
answers.answer: An action resolving with at least one ill district involved adds 2 threat total. A district is involved if chosen, or if a token/unit is placed there, removed from it, or moved into/out of it; even prevented placement/movement still involves the intended destination. Multiple ill districts do not multiply the 2. Production and event cards do not trigger the action illness effect. Illness reaching the Root separately returns to reserve and adds 2 threat.
evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Illness and involved districts: complete subsection.

answers.answer: Globalsec gains 1 capital per enemy unit removed from a district; Haas-Bioroid gains 2 when one or more androids move, at most once per turn; Jinteki gains 2 per illness token removed from a district; Melange, after resolving an event, gains 3 if threat did not increase by at least 2 over the entire event; NBN gains 1 per stage unrest decreases; Weyland gains 2 per outage removed from a district. Except Melange, contracts trigger only through resolving an action card, regardless of which player resolves it. Moving out of a district or returning something at the Root is not removal. Haas is once per turn regardless of number moved. Outage clearing unrest does not pay NBN. Melange includes event placements and Root movement in its threat check.
evidence: Corporation draws and contracts: complete contract table; preceding contract paragraph; event subsection paragraph on whole-event Melange check; Root paragraph on removal.

answers.answer: Players may trade capital, assets, and promises; gifts without return are legal. They cannot trade action cards, emergencies, investments, rivals, or corporation sheets. A trade all parties can immediately and completely fulfill is binding; three-or-more-player trades bind when every part resolves immediately and simultaneously. Future promises are nonbinding; if binding status is disputed before agreement, it is nonbinding. An exhausted asset remains exhausted when traded and does not ready on receipt.
evidence: Actions > Negotiation and trading: complete subsection, including FAQ correction and binding examples.

answers.answer: If one player controls multiple abilities with the same timing, they choose their order; when multiple players have same-timing assets, resolve clockwise from the active player. ‘May’ and End of Turn abilities are optional. Exhausted assets ready during Refresh, after start-of-turn triggers. A newly received asset with an End of Turn header may be used that turn. Use each End of Turn ability once per turn; additional acquisitions with that header during the step may also be used that turn.
evidence: Turn Structure > Standard round and active turn: complete End of Turn and Refresh rules; Special Rules & Edge Cases > Assets, claiming, exhaustion and theft: complete timing paragraph.

answers.answer: First reveal and score each investment using its printed award/formula/cap; a required resource below target yields zero. Then check all five supplies: if any is below target, demand fails and threat rises by the card's printed amount once; otherwise it succeeds. Next reset every resource to 0, put the old demand under its deck, reveal the next demand and set targets. Then return all investments to the deck and shuffle; each player draws two, keeps one facedown, and returns the other facedown to the top. On the third demand, after investment scoring and demand check the game ends; omit reset/reveal and investment choice.
evidence: Turn Structure > Demand round: complete numbered procedure.

answers.answer: Yes. Investment scoring precedes the final demand check, so it scores before failure raises threat to 25. At 25 threat, ordinary corporations lose; a Federalist with at least 25 capital wins. If the third demand ends below 25, a named-corporation rival requires strictly more capital than that corporation; a tie loses. With your own corporation as rival, you must strictly exceed at least 2 other players at four players, or at least 3 at five/six; tied players do not count as beaten. A Federalist rival loses below 25.
evidence: Turn Structure > Demand round: steps 1–2 and third-round exception; Scoring / Victory Conditions: complete table and explanatory paragraphs.

answers.answer: Players cannot tell others which actions are in their hands and cannot lie about hand counts; stolen/given actions remain secret. Rivals cannot be revealed or discussed. Chosen investments stay facedown until demand; unchosen investments are not revealed, and players do not inspect the deck after dealing. Do not inspect facedown turn-track assets. Event fronts seen via look/reorder stay secret; event backs, including the deck's top back, are public. Thomas Haas requires an open statement whether the player swaps the under-board rival with their own; whether a swap occurred is public, identities remain secret.
evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Discards, replenishment and information: complete subsection; FAQ & Rulings: complete Thomas Haas row.

answers.answer: Ordinary actions go facedown to the shared discard; discarded assets go facedown to the bottom of their asset deck; removed components return to reserve. If an action type is empty, shuffle the entire shared discard, reveal and sort by type, then shuffle each type into its own deck. If the reserve lacks a required component, do not place it. Supply tracks cap at their last numbered space. The summary does not specify an outcome for production exceeding the track end.
evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases > Discards, replenishment and information: complete replenishment paragraph; Components: reserve rule; Special Rules & Edge Cases > Production, unrest and outages: complete supply cap sentence. No rule stated for production beyond track end.

answers.answer: A standard round is Action, then Production, then Event. During Production exploit android districts in ascending district-number order, produce resources under existing modifiers, then increase unrest. Reveal the event; resolve upper effect, then one copy of each listed component in every district beside it, then its next turn count by placing that many assets from the top of the deck facedown starting at slot 1. Put the event on the bottom of its deck and advance the round marker. The turn track need not be reset after the sixth standard round because no Action Phase follows.
evidence: Turn Structure > Standard round and active turn; Production Phase; Event Phase: complete subsections.

answers.answer: Liquidation produces a district's resources without exploiting it: apply normal production modifiers, but not normal exploitation effects such as unrest increase. Caprice cannot affect Unorthodox Knowledge, and the player resolving Unorthodox Knowledge is not bound to resolve it the way they announced.
evidence: FAQ & Rulings: complete Liquidation row and complete Unorthodox Knowledge / Caprice Nisei row.
